title: Kinetic content manifest
description: The manifest.json of a Kinetic content folder. See docs/content-format.md for semantics.

$schema.description: optional address of the JSON Schema an editor checks this manifest against; kinetic-extract writes ./manifest.schema.json, a copy of this schema beside manifest.json; the player and validator ignore the value; see docs/content-format.md § Manifest

storyId.description: optional stable identity of the story, independent of where its folder lives; the player keys saved progress and bookmarks by it (absent: by the folder URL); see docs/content-format.md § Manifest

title.description: optional name of the game, shown as a heading at the top of the player's Esc help screen and as the page title (absent: no heading); plain text, never HTML; see docs/content-format.md § Manifest

version.description: optional release of the game as its author names it (1.2, 0.9 beta, Episode 3), shown after the title on the player's Esc help screen; plain text, never HTML; not the format's schemaVersion; see docs/content-format.md § Manifest

items.description: an empty items array is valid: it is an honestly-empty folder (no visual of the sliced flow resolved to a file), and the player shows its no-content state for it (docs/extracting.md BUG 1)

branches.description: optional table of branch decisions over the item array; a decision fires on the forward settle of its `after` item and offers 2..N contiguous route spans; see docs/content-format.md § Branches

audio.description: optional sound; a manifest without it plays silent; see docs/content-format.md § Audio

tracks.description: track id -> track; items name tracks by these ids, which the validator resolves; several ids may share one file

voices.description: optional speaker name -> voice, the reference clip spoken lines in that speaker's voice are generated from on the reader's machine; keys are speaker names exactly as items' `speaker` gives them; the validator warns about a voice no item's speaker uses; see docs/content-format.md § Voices

narrator.description: optional voice for items that have text but no speaker; see docs/content-format.md § Voices

durationSeconds.description: the track's length; authoritative, the player never reads the audio element's duration (WebKit misreports Ogg durations)

startSeconds.description: where a play starts; default 0; less than durationSeconds, which the validator enforces

loopStartSeconds.description: where a loop restarts; default: the track's startSeconds, so a loop restarts where the track started; less than durationSeconds, which the validator enforces

loop.description: whether the track loops when it plays as music or ambience; default true

file.description: the reference clip: about 10 to 13 seconds of clean speech; an audio file with its script beside it, as a track's file (FLAC or WAV keeps it lossless)

text.description: optional transcript of the reference clip

description.description: optional description the voice was designed from

itemAudioFields.description: the audio fields every item type takes; itemAudio and videoItemAudio close the set

music.description: the music from this item on: a track id, or null to stop it; the validator resolves the id

ambience.description: the whole set of ambience loops from this item on, distinct track ids (the validator enforces both); [] stops them all

fadeMs.description: fade for this item's music and ambience changes, in milliseconds; default 1000

voice.description: track id of the item's voice line; the validator resolves it

track.description: track id of the one-shot; the validator resolves it

delayMs.description: wait before the one-shot starts, in milliseconds; default 0

channel.description: a one-shot on a channel stops the one already playing on it; without a channel, one-shots overlap

videoSound.description: a video item's own sound, played as a separate track whose time is the video's media time; the track must be at least as long as the item's range end, within 0.05 s, which the validator enforces

duck.description: scales music and ambience while the video sound plays; default 1

id.description: decision id; unique across branches and distinct from every item id, which the validator enforces

after.description: item id the decision fires on: when this item settles (forward), the overlay opens; must resolve to an item id, which the validator enforces

prompt.description: question shown above the route list; the validator caps its length

continuingRoute.description: id of the one route that continues the story; it must name a route of this decision and require continueAt, which the validator enforces

continueAt.description: item id where the continuing route proceeds after its end; allowed only with continuingRoute and must resolve to an item after every route end, which the validator enforces

id.description: route id; unique within its decision, which the validator enforces

label.description: text shown in the route list; the validator caps its length

start.description: first item of the route's inclusive contiguous span; must resolve to an item id at or before `end`, after the decision's `after` item, which the validator enforces

end.description: last item of the route's span; must resolve to an item id

result.description: what happens when the route ends: "ending" means its last item IS the ending (no implicit join); "return" needs the decision's continuingRoute and offers return-to-main via continueAt; "continue" proceeds to the decision's continueAt after the route, as the continuing route does (under Play all routes it re-offers the choice while a route of the decision is unplayed this pass), and needs continuingRoute/continueAt, which the validator enforces; default "ending"

path.description: a media file's path relative to the content folder root, forward-slash separated. Every segment is [A-Za-z0-9._-] and starts with a letter or digit, so there are no empty or dot-leading segments, no "..", no absolute path, no backslash, no drive letter or URL scheme, and no whitespace. Subfolders (the converter writes `media/<h[:2]>/<h>.<ext>`, `h` the sha256 of the shipped bytes) are allowed and optional; the last segment is still a flat file name — an id-shaped stem (a 64-hex digest fits), at most one derivative suffix (`.fNNN`, `.poster`, `.thumb`), then the extension. `imagePath` adds the browser image format extension list, `audioPath` the audio one; `videoPath` adds none.

videoPath.description: a video file: any extension. There is no video extension list of our own; the converter ships whatever its measured playability rule keeps (docs/plan.md Phase 26) at the true container's usual extension (mp4, mov, m4v, 3gp, webm, mkv).

audioPath.description: an audio file: mp3, m4a, wav, flac or webm. Ogg (ogg, oga, opus) passes the schema, and the validator warns about it: Safari plays Ogg only from 18.4 (macOS 15.4) and WebKit's decode of Vorbis in Ogg loses its first 128 samples.

thought.description: true marks text as the speaker's unspoken thought rather than spoken dialogue; requires a non-empty text, which the validator enforces
true marks text as the speaker's unspoken thought rather than spoken dialogue; requires a non-empty text, which the validator enforces

startSeconds.description: playback range start in exact fractional seconds, never rounded; default 0; endSeconds > startSeconds and endSeconds <= durationSeconds are cross-field rules the validator enforces (docs/content-format.md, Video playback ranges)

endSeconds.description: playback range end in exact fractional seconds, never rounded; default durationSeconds; endSeconds > startSeconds and endSeconds <= durationSeconds are cross-field rules the validator enforces (docs/content-format.md, Video playback ranges)

loopStartSeconds.description: loop restart point in exact fractional seconds, never rounded; default startSeconds, so only the first pass plays the pre-roll; must be less than the effective end (endSeconds if present, else durationSeconds), a cross-field rule the validator enforces (docs/content-format.md, Video playback ranges)

segments.description: the camera views of the file in order, which Space steps through after the item's lines (docs/content-format.md, Video segments); each starts at or after the end of the one before (touching allowed), a cross-field rule the validator enforces; the times are file times, free of the item's own range

loopCount.description: times the video plays before auto-advance; default 1

holdSeconds.description: explicit display duration; when present the media gate is time driven and ended is ignored (docs/content-format.md, Timing)

minPlaySeconds.description: floor for chain-exit timing: in auto mode the player waits at the end of the video's dialogue chain until minPlaySeconds have elapsed since the chain's video item became current; manual advance and skip stay immediate; outside chains it has no effect beyond the media gate (docs/content-format.md, Timing)

thought.description: true marks text as the speaker's unspoken thought rather than spoken dialogue; requires a non-empty text, which the validator enforces

videoSegment.description: one view of a video item's file; values in exact fractional seconds, never rounded

loopStartSeconds.description: where the view's loop restarts; default the segment's startSeconds; below startSeconds is legal; less than endSeconds, which the validator enforces

endSeconds.description: where the view ends; greater than startSeconds and at most the item's durationSeconds, which the validator enforces

thought.description: true marks text as the speaker's unspoken thought rather than spoken dialogue; requires a non-empty text, which the validator enforces
